summary.headline: 3i Infotech Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 4.3% YoY to ₹177.9 crore, with gross margin up to 14.4% and TCV of ₹240.9 crore.
summary.overview: Operating revenue was ₹177.9 crore, up 4.3% YoY and 1.3% QoQ, with gross margin improving to 14.4% from 12.6% in Q4 FY26. EBITDA was ₹11.5 crore and PAT ₹6.5 crore, against a prior-year quarter inflated by ₹18.5 crore pre-tax one-time US ECS income. Management said forex contributed only ₹4 crore this quarter, so profit is more operating-driven. Order booking was ₹240.9 crore TCV, of which about ₹80 crore were renewals. Management declined to give revenue guidance but reiterated a ₹2,000 crore revenue vision for 2030 and said it needs about 30% CAGR.

financial_highlights.change: from 12.6% in Q4 FY26 and 11.2% a year earlier
prior-year quarter included ₹18.5 crore pre-tax one-time other income
prior-year quarter included ₹13.5 crore post-tax one-time ECS credit
Q4 FY26 included ~₹15 crore forex revaluation gain
down from ₹25 crore in Q4 FY26 and ₹18 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Application, Automation and Analytics (AAA)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 73.5% of Q1 revenue; focus on application modernization, data and analytics, AI-led solutions and ERP transformation.

segments.name: Infrastructure Services (IS)
segments.commentary: 18.7% of Q1 revenue; steady execution across cloud, cybersecurity, hybrid infrastructure and managed services.

segments.name: Business Process Services (BPS)
segments.commentary: 7.8% of Q1 revenue; management called the operating environment challenging but cited early signs of progress from transformation and expansion beyond domestic BFSI into the US, Middle East and other verticals.

segments.name: Geography: India
segments.commentary: ₹66.6 crore, up from ₹63.5 crore in Q4 FY26 (+4.9% QoQ).

segments.name: Geography: US
segments.commentary: ₹91.2 crore, down 7.2% QoQ from ₹98.3 crore, attributed by management to project timing and seasonality.

segments.name: Geography: Middle East
segments.commentary: ₹15.9 crore, up 64% QoQ from ₹9.7 crore on new business wins.

guidance_outlook: No revenue guidance given; management said it does not publish forward revenue numbers.
Vision 2030 target of ₹2,000 crore revenue (management said ₹2030 crore in one place but confirmed ₹2,000 crore); internal CAGR target is about 30%.
Management expects remaining ~₹160 crore of non-renewal TCV to start kicking in from Q2 FY27 onward; more traction expected from next quarter.
Other expenses expected to stay in the ₹14-15 crore per quarter range unless revenue scales toward ₹2,000 crore, or with another 25-30% revenue growth.
Management said roughly 90%+ probability of renewal on annually renewed contracts, giving at least 12 months of visibility; FY27 and FY28 internal plans are on track.
Annual salary increment planned for October, in line with the October-September cycle.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.

Expanded Centre of Excellence, technology partnerships and AI-enabled capabilities; over 150 data and advanced analytics professionals and over 350 certified automation and quality engineering specialists serving 100-plus customers.
Established local leadership teams in Canada and East Africa during the quarter.
Carved out a ~30-year-old RTA business (annual revenue ~₹6 crore) into a wholly owned subsidiary, NuRe Future Tech, as an internal restructuring to meet regulatory net-worth requirements.
demand_pricing: Order booking of ₹240.9 crore TCV and ₹195.6 crore ACV, with 25+ new client wins; about ₹80 crore were renewals. Cumulative order book stated at about ₹400 crore.
Management said most AAA, staff augmentation and IS contracts are renewed annually, with some customers relationships of 5-10 years.
New focus areas identified about 7-8 months ago: ERP (SAP, Oracle; starting from zero base), cloud, cybersecurity, and AI/ML/blockchain/IoT.
Partnerships with SAP (US), Oracle (Middle East and India), Microsoft and hyperscalers.
Management will keep pursuing small orders (₹6-8 crore) alongside large ones; announcements are made only for orders of ₹1 crore and above.
Management said the sales funnel is healthier across all four geographies under the new leadership team, but did not disclose its size.

qa_highlights.question: Are revenues set to improve from Q2 given TCV wins, and are projects on hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue has moved from ₹170-175 crore range to ₹175-180 crore over the last two quarters. Remaining non-renewal projects start from Q2 depending on implementation timing; traction expected to rise quarter on quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the e-Mudhra case and the Capital Next 5% stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Case is under EOW investigation with statements recorded; no formal talks with e-Mudhra. Capital Next and acting-in-concert parties are from the same family group, so e-Mudhra has indirectly acquired over 5%. Management said the shareholding and legal case are separate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall, and what run rate should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost cuts through office consolidation and lower consultant, advisory and travel costs. Q4 FY26 had ~₹5.5-6 crore old service tax provision and ~₹3 crore book clean-up. Expect ₹14-15 crore per quarter, rising only with scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 2030 target, the order book and the CAGR needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Vision 2030 target is ₹2,000 crore; management would not give yearly guidance but has a Board-approved trajectory. Management said 30% growth is needed to reach the target and the internal target is that CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: Which of the focus areas will become top-tier, and what is the SAP strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too small to target number one or two positions and will focus on four or five areas: ERP, cloud, cybersecurity and AI/ML/blockchain/IoT. Analyst asked for a 3-5 year plan; management agreed.

qa_highlights.question: Will larger orders replace smaller ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep pursuing both; smaller orders help start customer relationships. Large-order teams are separate. Small-order discipline may come only after reaching ₹2,000 crore scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the RailTel dispute?
qa_highlights.answer: Arbitration is invoked; statement of claim, counterclaim and defence are filed; hearings expected next month. Management does not expect a quick result. Equivalent provisions have been made, so no further balance sheet exposure is seen.

risks_watch: Revenue has been flat at ₹170-180 crore for about six quarters; the ₹240.9 crore TCV needs to convert into revenue from Q2 onward.
US revenue fell 7.2% QoQ; watch for recovery given it is the largest market.
BPS remains challenging per management; no segment numbers beyond revenue share.
Vision 2030 requires about 25-30% CAGR, so a weak FY27 would add pressure later.
Forex and one-time income no longer support profit; watch for sustained operating margin.
RailTel arbitration could take years; provisions are in place but the case is unresolved.
e-Mudhra criminal investigation (EOW) and its indirect 5%+ shareholding through the Capital Next group.
A cybersecurity incident occurred this quarter; management said there was no material impact.
Management's new focus areas are at zero or small base (ERP), so growth from them is unproven.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, execution and the 2030 vision, but evasive on forward numbers, declining to give revenue guidance or a yearly revenue path. Management was candid that revenue growth is modest ("not a major improvement") and deflected sharply on the e-Mudhra matter and the RailTel arbitration.
key_quotes: While It is not a major improvement, I agree, but at least the needle has moved from ₹170 crore levels to ₹180 crore.
We do not have either the forex gains or any other one-time income events contributing in this quarter.
If we are to achieve our vision the 2030, we cannot afford to have less than 30% growth for sure.
We currently have no presence in this space, so whatever we build from now onwards will represent significant growth because our base is zero.

growth.why: No revenue guidance given; management reiterated a ₹2,000 crore Vision 2030 target (~30% CAGR) and said ~₹160 crore of non-renewal TCV should start contributing from Q2 FY27, backed by ₹240.9 crore TCV booking and ~₹400 crore cumulative order book, but no capacity additions or capex were discussed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose to 14.4% from 12.6% in Q4 FY26 and 11.2% a year earlier, and other expenses fell to ₹13 crore from ₹25 crore, but EBITDA of ₹11.5 crore on ₹177.9 crore revenue (~6.5%) has no guided path and forex no longer props profit.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity or plant additions were discussed; only an expanded Centre of Excellence and a RTA business carve-out into NuRe Future Tech (~₹6 crore revenue) for regulatory net-worth reasons.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue rose 4.3% YoY to ₹177.9 crore, and about ₹160 crore of non-renewal TCV from the ₹240.9 crore booking is expected to start contributing from Q2 FY27, but revenue has been flat at ₹170-180 crore for about six quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no revenue guidance and declined to publish forward numbers, while calling revenue growth 'not a major improvement'.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The ~30% CAGR needed for the ₹2,000 crore 2030 vision is far above the 4.3% YoY growth delivered, and the US business fell 7.2% QoQ to ₹91.2 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Focus areas (ERP on SAP and Oracle, cloud, cybersecurity, AI/ML/blockchain/IoT) and partnerships with SAP, Oracle, Microsoft and hyperscalers were named, but no specific product launch dates were given and the ERP base is zero.

rows.label: Conversion of ₹240.9 crore TCV into revenue
rows.why: About ₹160 crore of non-renewal TCV is expected to kick in from Q2 FY27, against a cumulative order book of about ₹400 crore, with 25+ new client wins and ₹195.6 crore ACV.

rows.label: Middle East growth on new wins
rows.why: Middle East revenue rose 64% QoQ to ₹15.9 crore from ₹9.7 crore on new business wins, and the sales funnel is described as healthier across all four geographies.

rows.label: Other expenses held at ₹14-15 crore per quarter
rows.why: Other expenses fell to ₹13 crore from ₹25 crore in Q4 FY26 through office consolidation and lower consultant, advisory and travel costs, and are expected to stay at ₹14-15 crore a quarter unless revenue scales.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, execution and the ₹2,000 crore 2030 vision, but candid that revenue growth is modest and declined to give revenue guidance; analysts pressed on the e-Mudhra shareholding and investigation and the RailTel arbitration, which management deflected.
